name: Livonian
catalog_quote: With the exception of a few monosyllabic words that may be unstressed in the sentence, a word has at least one stressed syllable. The primary stress in Livonian is on the first syllable of a word. This is valid also for foreign words. ... If a prosodic word has four or more syllables, the secondary stress is usually on the third syllable of a word
sweep_summary: One works with stress in the title: Tuisk 2015 'Livonian word prosody' is the Tartu PhD dissertation (DSpace handle 10062/48857; 54-page summary without appended articles), downloaded open and read. Its p. 31 statement — primary stress on the first syllable, secondary stress usually on the third, -nikā affix exception — confirms the catalog's fixed-strict coding and is a summary of its paper [P4], i.e. the catalog's deciding source Tuisk 2015 LU LI(3):177-195. That article was also downloaded from kirj.ee (open) and the catalog's domain_quote checked verbatim at pp. 177-178 (initial primary stress also in loans; secondary on syllable 3 for 4+ syllables; trisyllabic final secondary foot in odd-length words of 5+; -nikā and late-loan long-vowel exceptions; Latvian-borrowed short verb prefixes unstressed). No contradiction, no refinement beyond what the catalog already flags; nothing left unread; no acquisition priority. Note for the per-language bibliography: item 6 there gives the dissertation as 'Tuisk (2016)'; the record is dated 2015-10-12 (issued 2015). discovery was done via the DSpace REST API, Crossref and Semantic Scholar APIs.

sources.quote: Paper [P4] analyzed Livonian trisyllabic, tetrasyllabic and pentasyllabic words with various structures with the focus on non-initial syllables and secondary-stressed feet. The primary stress in Livonian is on the first syllable of a word and the secondary stress is usually on the third syllable of a word. However, in the derivational affix -nikā the secondary stress can be on the second syllable of a word. (p. 31) ... Livonian has preserved the main prosodic features characteristic of Finnic languages, such as (a) word-initial stress and (b) the phonological opposition of short and long phoneme duration. (p. 24)
sources.locator: p. 31, section 4.1.3 'Temporal structure of tri-, tetra- and pentasyllabic words'; also p. 24, section 4.1.1; p. 17, section 3.1.1 'Stress' (generic definitions only)
sources.note: Primary stress fixed on the first syllable; secondary stress usually on the third syllable; the derivational affix -nikā can pull secondary stress onto the second syllable. The thesis is an acoustic study of quantity, foot isochrony and stød; its stress-placement content is a compressed restatement of its constituent article [P4] = Tuisk 2015, Linguistica Uralica LI(3) 177-195, which is the catalog's deciding source. Section 3.1.1 'Stress' (p. 17) is general background with no Livonian-specific placement statement.

sources.quote: With the exception of a few monosyllabic words that may be unstressed in the sentence, a word has at least one stressed syllable. The primary stress in Livonian is on the first syllable of a word. This is valid also for foreign words. Only short-syllable verb prefixes borrowed from Latvian can be unstressed, e.g. no|võ·ttõ 'remove, Inf'. ... If a prosodic word has four or more syllables, the secondary stress is usually on the third syllable of a word (pie·dāgõ:dõn 'pine, DPl'). If a word has five syllables or a larger odd number of syllables, the secondary-stressed foot is usually trisyllabic (o·pāti:jizõn 'teacher, DSg').
sources.note: Primary stress initial (also in loans); secondary stress usually on syllable 3 in words of 4+ syllables; in odd-length words of 5+ syllables the final secondary foot is trisyllabic (10100, 1010100); exceptions: -nikā affix takes secondary stress on syllable 2 'in all cases', late loanwords with a long non-initial vowel can carry secondary stress (ka·ptē:n, be·nzī:n), compounds keep each component's pattern. Verbatim match to the catalog's domain_quote and to its stress placement coded per word length as 10 100 1010 10100 101010 1010100 10101010 (1 = a stressed syllable).

sources.quote: "The prosodic system of Livonian ... is based on syllable weight. The basic foot in these languages is the MORAIC TROCHEE. All these languages also share the undominated constraint that words are stressed on the initial syllable." Confirms initial primary stress; says nothing about the position of secondary stress in 4+ syllable words.
